clue.text: Joseph to praise the unemployed

parts.note: Jo is a short form of the name Joseph
to bless is to praise or glorify

explanation.surface: Someone named Joseph is urged to sing the praises of people out of work.
explanation.definitionFit: People without work are described collectively as the jobless, so the adjective stands in for 'the unemployed'.

clue.text: Heavenly body looking good in sacking rebel leader

indicators.note: the words for looking good go inside the word for sacking

parts.note: jute is the coarse fibre used to make sacking
PI, short for pious, describes someone who looks virtuous or sanctimonious

indicators.note: the leader of a word is its first letter, here of rebel

explanation.surface: A rebel leader is dismissed yet still looks saintly, as if blessed by the heavens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sacking' suggests firing someone; here it is the cloth JUTE. PI (pious) goes inside, then R from 'rebel leader' ends it.
explanation.definitionFit: A planet is a heavenly body, and this one is the largest in the solar system.

clue.text: European feature having a slippery slope?

definitions.text: European feature having a slippery slope?

parts.words: European feature having a slippery slope?
parts.note: reads as a ski slope in the Alps, but means a huge EU stockpile of a greasy dairy product, which is a slippery heap

explanation.surface: An Alpine landmark with a treacherous incline.
explanation.walkthrough: The European Community's agricultural policy produced vast surplus stores of dairy produce, nicknamed after mountains; one of greasy spread would indeed be slippery.
explanation.definitionFit: The surplus stockpile of a dairy fat built up under EU farm subsidies was likened to a mountain range feature.

clue.text: Never heartlessly confused by a bird

indicators.note: confused means the remaining letters are jumbled into a new order
without its heart means the middle letter of Never is removed

explanation.surface: Someone is told they will never be bewildered by a bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heartlessly' takes the middle V out of NEVER, leaving NEER; 'confused' rearranges NEER.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a sea eagle, a crossword staple among birds of prey.

clue.text: Quiet, having been overpowered

explanation.surface: A person falls silent after being beaten.
explanation.definitionFit: Muted describes something quiet in tone, and a conquered force has been brought under control: both senses share the word.

clue.text: Bruce has no right to rearrange the body

indicators.note: the letters left over are to be rearranged into another order
has no means the letter for right is dropped from Bruce

explanation.surface: Bruce, lacking the authority, cannot reorganise the governing body.
explanation.walkthrough: 'has no right' removes R from BRUCE, leaving BUCE; 'to rearrange' mixes those letters. 'body' is meant in the geometric sense of a solid.
explanation.definitionFit: In geometry a solid figure with six square faces is a body or solid.

clue.text: One way to convey news

parts.note: a route or medium through which information passes, such as a television station or a line of communication

explanation.definitionFit: A medium or conduit for passing on information, as in a TV station or a route of communication.

clue.text: Better that non-drinker leaves this

indicators.note: leaves means the letters for the non-drinker depart from the word Better

parts.note: TT means teetotal, a person who drinks no alcohol

explanation.surface: A teetotaller had best stay away from this drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leaves' takes TT out of BETTER. The whole clue also defines: a non-drinker would naturally leave this beverage alone.
explanation.definitionFit: The whole clue describes an alcoholic drink that a teetotaller avoids, like ale or lager.

clue.text: Flower faeries dancing

indicators.note: dancing means the letters of faeries move about into a new order

explanation.surface: Fairies dance among the flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: A fragrant plant of the iris family grown for its bell-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Not being a regular worker, does he not take his job seriously?

definitions.text: does he not take his job seriously?

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether a temporary hand is simply too laid-back about the work.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the first word as 'nonchalant': a worker who is offhand about his labour.
explanation.definitionFit: A hired hand engaged by the day rather than on staff, and, reading the first word as offhand, a worker who is relaxed about the job.

clue.text: Assume a Red Indian mask and do not let the tears show

definitions.text: do not let the tears show

explanation.surface: Someone dons a warrior's disguise and holds back their crying.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading takes 'brave' as the old term for a Native American warrior, so the phrase means wearing his face.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally donning a warrior's face, and idiomatically acting cheerful despite distress.

clue.text: They object

parts.note: reads as people protesting, but means the grammatical object form of the pronoun 'they'

explanation.definitionFit: The objective case of the third person plural pronoun, used where 'they' is the grammatical object.

clue.text: At least two of the five being of the same age

definitions.text: At least two of the five being of the same age

parts.words: At least two of the five being of the same age
parts.note: five babies born at one birth are all the same age, so any two of them share it

explanation.definitionFit: Short for quintuplets, five siblings born together in one delivery.

clue.text: No variety actor to put across the cat in pantomime

definitions.text: No variety actor to put across the cat in pantomime

parts.words: No variety actor to put across the cat in pantomime
parts.note: a performer plays the feline character of a Christmas pantomime, as in the tale of the cat in boots

explanation.walkthrough: British pantomime is a Christmas stage show based on fairy tales; the cat in Boots is a stock role.
explanation.definitionFit: A familiar name for a cat, and the title character of a Christmas pantomime tale about a booted feline.

clue.text: Leave no capital

parts.note: to quit is to leave or depart
O is nought, a zero or nothing

explanation.surface: An order to stay out of the capital.
explanation.definitionFit: The capital city of Ecuador, high in the Andes.

clue.text: Loosely this is designed to cover other clothing

definitions.text: Loosely this is designed to cover other clothing

parts.words: Loosely this is designed to cover other clothing
parts.note: a loose overgarment worn over everyday clothes to protect them

explanation.definitionFit: A loose overall garment, as worn by artists or farm workers, put on over other clothes.

clue.text: In a short time ruled out this type of tyre

indicators.note: the words for a short time sit inside the rearranged letters
out means the letters of ruled are jumbled

parts.note: MO, short for moment, is a brief time

explanation.surface: A tyre that was rejected almost immediately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges RULED into REULD, and 'In' puts MO inside it after RE.
explanation.definitionFit: A retread: a worn tyre given a new tread moulded onto its old casing.

clue.text: Hit topless girl with a thin plate

parts.note: to lam is to thrash or hit

indicators.note: topless means the first letter of the girl's name is removed

parts.note: Bella is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A semi-naked girl is struck with a slender dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the B from BELLA, leaving ELLA.
explanation.definitionFit: A thin layer, membrane or scale, as in the gills of a mushroom.

clue.text: Going the other way in a shop

explanation.surface: Someone walks against the flow through a store.
explanation.definitionFit: Contrary or opposite in direction, and the long table across which goods are sold in a store.

clue.text: Member in potentially cruel surroundings to give way

indicators.note: the word for a member goes inside the rearranged letters
potentially means the letters of cruel could form another word when shuffled

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician gives in when surrounded by people who could turn nasty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potentially' turns CRUEL into CRULE; 'in ... surroundings' puts MP inside it after CRU.
explanation.definitionFit: To collapse or buckle, as a person might fold under pressure.

clue.text: Reckless motorist, a swine, getting under way

indicators.note: in a down entry the word for swine is placed below the word for way

parts.note: a road is a way
a hog is a pig or swine

explanation.surface: A careless driver is called a pig as he gets moving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting under way' sounds like setting off; in a down clue the HOG sits under ROAD.
explanation.definitionFit: A driver who selfishly hogs the highway and drives without consideration.

clue.text: Stupid person, sailor alongside a ship!

parts.note: Jack, or Jack tar, is a sailor
SS stands for steamship

explanation.surface: A deckhand standing by a vessel is called an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: A male donkey, used as an insult for a fool.

clue.text: After about 15 days of early summer, I just arranged my defence

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters follow the shortened month
half the days of the month, so only the first half of the month's name is kept

parts.note: June is a month of early summer

indicators.note: arranged means the letters of I just are put in a fresh order

explanation.surface: Someone trains in a martial art for a fortnight as summer begins.
explanation.walkthrough: June has 30 days, so 'about 15 days' keeps half its name, JU; 'arranged' turns IJUST into JITSU.
explanation.definitionFit: A Japanese art of unarmed self-defence using holds and throws.

clue.text: Racket that should be taken to court

definitions.text: Racket that should be taken to court

parts.words: Racket that should be taken to court
parts.note: reads as tennis equipment, but means a fraudulent scheme that belongs in a courtroom

explanation.definitionFit: A fraud or confidence trick, the kind of dishonest scheme prosecuted in law.

clue.text: Capable of scheming

explanation.surface: Someone able to plot.
explanation.definitionFit: Equal to a task, and engaged in mischief, as in 'what are you plotting?'.

clue.text: Do not allow the girl to play this instrument

parts.note: to ban is to prohibit
Jo is a girl's name

explanation.surface: Someone is told to forbid a girl from playing an instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: A stringed folk instrument with a round drum-like body.

clue.text: One marshy area back in the desert

indicators.note: back means the joined words are read in reverse order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
a bog is a marsh

explanation.surface: A lone swamp lies back in the desert.
explanation.walkthrough: I plus BOG gives IBOG, which 'back' turns round.
explanation.definitionFit: A vast desert spanning Mongolia and northern China.

clue.text: Leading player among the first arrivals

indicators.note: among means the letters are found inside the run of first arrivals

explanation.surface: The lead performer is one of the earliest to turn up.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal performer, the headline name in a cast.

clue.text: Endless swagger by a bird

indicators.note: endless means the final letter of the synonym is removed

parts.note: swank is boastful swagger or showing off

explanation.surface: A bird struts about without end.
explanation.definitionFit: A large white waterbird with a long graceful neck.

clue.text: Put up left-wing slogans and celebrate

explanation.surface: Activists daub political graffiti and then party.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading is literal: covering the town in the colour of socialism.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally daubing a city in the colour of the left, and idiomatically going on a wild night out.

clue.text: I leave the boy on the cliff

indicators.note: leave means the letter I goes away from the boy's name

parts.note: Craig is a boy's name

explanation.surface: A speaker abandons a lad on a clifftop.
explanation.definitionFit: A steep rugged rock face.

clue.text: Upset one in Lyons never mucking about

parts.note: un is French for one, and Lyons is a French city

indicators.note: mucking about means the letters of never are messed around

explanation.surface: Someone in Lyons never fooling around is unsettling.
explanation.definitionFit: To unsettle or rattle someone, robbing them of courage.
